# RootVine

> Neutral product and media resolution for AI agents, delivered as an MCP server. Ask where to stream, buy or collect something and get back ranked options with direct links — ordered by trust, price and availability, never by commission.

RootVine is a thin client. It holds no ranking logic and caches nothing: every call fetches live data at request time, so an answer is only as old as the source behind it.

Music is live today. Further categories are added only once a source can answer them properly — a tool that is registered but not yet active says so rather than returning empty results.

Outbound links are returned as tracked click URLs, and some carry affiliate codes. Only a tracked click URL can lead to a tagged page; the plain `url` in each result never carries an affiliate code. Affiliate relationships never influence ranking: commission fields are excluded from the ranking function by design, and that exclusion is enforced by tests.

## Install

- Hosted, nothing to install: add `https://mcp.rootvine.ai/mcp` as a remote MCP server (streamable HTTP, no login, no key) in any client that accepts one, such as a claude.ai custom connector.
- [npm: rootvine-mcp](https://www.npmjs.com/package/rootvine-mcp): run with `npx -y rootvine-mcp`. Works over stdio in any MCP client.
- [Source, MIT licence](https://github.com/RagingOrangutan/rootvine-mcp): full source, release notes and issue tracker.

## Tools

Pass the user's own words as `query` ("galway girl by ed sheeran", "what albums has Stromae released") — never build slugs. RootVine finds the page. `slug` still works as a deprecated alias for `query`.

- `find_product`: start here when the category is unclear. Reads music or games from the words (keyword-based — set `category` when you know it) and answers in that tool's shape.
- `resolve_music`: where to stream, buy digitally, or collect a track or album on physical media — streaming services, digital stores, vinyl, CD and collector listings, ranked. A typo is corrected and flagged in `resolved_as`; a miss returns `did_you_mean`: close matches, each with a `query` to pass back. A title several artists recorded, asked without an artist, returns those recordings to choose from rather than one picked at random.
- `resolve_artist`: an artist's profile and full discography, found by name. Each release comes back with a `query` that `resolve_music` turns into links. Physical formats are album-level, so this is the route to collector editions.
- `discover_music`: browse curated collections — charts, genre walls, moods, editorial playlists and spotlights — plus frozen chart snapshots back to 1946. Answers questions like "what was number one in 1994"; add `resolve` (true) with a `wall` to get number one's links in the same call.
- `resolve_game`: registered but not yet active. Returns an explicit "coming soon" response, with no links or prices, until the games source is live.

## How to read a response

RootVine never fabricates. Every link existed at resolved_at.

- Every answer comes as text plus `structuredContent` (MCP structured output) carrying the same facts: `status`, `results`, `partial_sources`, `resolved_as`, `did_you_mean`, `resolved_at` and `response_id`. Failures are plain-text errors.
- Every ranked result carries a structured `ranking_reason` with a code and a plain summary, so the ordering can be explained to a user rather than taken on trust.
- `status` is `success`, `partial` or `no_results`. A `partial` result is real but incomplete — `partial_sources` says which sources did not answer — and is labelled as such rather than presented as complete. On `no_results`, tell the user plainly and never fall back to guessing a link.
- When `resolved_as.corrected` is true, the answer is for different words than were asked: tell the user which recording is shown.
- Missing prices are `null`, never estimated. Zero results are an empty list, never fabricated.
- Limits: UK-focused stores and prices in GBP; music only today.
- Prefer `click_url` over `url` when both are present.
